paper_summary: The study analyzes a complex solar event on 2005-01-17 involving two fast CMEs that interacted in interplanetary space and multiple radio burst episodes (type III, type II, and type IV). Primary data sources include ground-based metric radio spectrography (ARTEMIS-IV), space-based low-frequency radio observations (Wind/WAVES and its TNR receiver), SOHO/LASCO coronagraph imaging, GOES soft X-ray fluxes, RSTN 15.4 GHz microwave fluxes, and in-situ energetic electron measurements by ACE/EPAM (with ACE/SWEPAM solar wind speeds). The results hinge on timing and spectral diagnostics across 650 MHz–20 kHz radio bands, CME kinematics from LASCO, SXR/microwave profiles for flare staging, and near-relativistic electron intensities and anisotropies at 1 AU. Key observation periods include flare stages and type III groups (09:07–09:28 UT, 09:43–09:59 UT), CME signatures (LASCO detections at 09:30 and 09:54 UT, heights at 11:30 UT), a distinct low-frequency type III group near 11:30 UT associated with CME interaction, and ACE/EPAM electron rises at ~10:00 UT and ~12:00 UT.

instruments.name: ARTEMIS-IV solar radio-spectrograph on board [Facility: ARTEMIS-IV]
instruments.general_comments: ARTEMIS-IV provided dynamic spectra in the metric range to identify and analyze type III bursts (III1, III2), type II emission, and an extended type IV continuum with fine structures, including high-resolution observations revealing pulsations, fiber bursts, and zebra patterns.
general_quotes: There we present the dynamic flux density spectrum of the radio bursts in the 650 MHz-20 kHz range (heliocentric distance ≈1.1 R⊙to 1 AU) using combined recordings of the Appareil de Routine pour le Traitement et l’Enregistrement Magn´etique de l’Information Spectrale (ARTEMIS-IV) solar radio-spectrograph (Caroubalos et al., 2001; Kontogeorgos et al., 2006) and the Wind/WAVES experiment (Bougeret et al., 1995).

data_collection_periods.period_name: Type III1 metric counterpart and fine structures
data_collection_periods.wavelengths: 200–500 MHz; 290–415 MHz; up to 630 MHz for combined context
wavelength_quotes: From the high-resolution observations in the 200- 500 MHz range (see figures 5, 6 for example)  it appears that most bursts are broadband pulsations.
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: Type III bursts with high-frequency fine structures (pulsations, RS and ordinary-drift bursts, fiber bursts) superposed on type IV continuum
physobs_quotes: Among these fine structures were broadband pulsations, bursts with ordinary and reverse drift, and fiber bursts due to whistlers travelling upwards in the corona (see Figure 5, e.g., 09:16:20-09:16:45 UT).
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: ARTEMIS-IV captured the evolving spectral character across the CME1 track, differentiating low- and high-frequency behaviors during III1.

data_collection_periods.period_name: Type III2 metric counterpart and fine structures
data_collection_periods.wavelengths: 300–400 MHz; up to 630 MHz for combined context
wavelength_quotes: The high-resolution spectrogram in the 300-400 MHz range (Fig. 6) shows a wealth of individual bursts with different drift rates and zebra pattern.
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: Type III bursts with mixed drift signatures; zebra pattern; activity indicating acceleration below CME front and onset of DH type III bursts
physobs_quotes: A close look at the dynamic spectrum (bottom panel of Figure 4) reveals negative overall drifts below 100 MHz, while burst groups with positive overall drift prevailed above 130 MHz.
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: ARTEMIS-IV documented the spectral complexity during stage 2, complementing DH observations.

time_quotes: The type IV continuum started near 08:40 UT during the initial smooth increase of the SXR flux before stage 1.
data_collection_periods.wavelengths: Metric range extending down to 5 MHz
wavelength_quotes: It dominated the metre wave spectrum during and after Type III2, and gradually penetrated to lower frequencies, down to 5 MHz.
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: Broadband type IV continuum with fine structures (pulsations, spikes, fiber bursts, zebra patterns)
physobs_quotes: From the high-resolution observations in the 200- 500 MHz range (see figures 5, 6 for example)  it appears that most bursts are broadband pulsations.
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: Type IV persisted throughout both flare stages, indicating ongoing coronal acceleration.

instruments.name: Wind/WAVES (including TNR) on board Wind
instruments.general_comments: Wind/WAVES provided decametric–kilometric dynamic spectra, identifying two major type III groups (III1, III2), the low-frequency type III3 near CME interaction, merged/continuing type II emission, Langmuir wave packets near the local plasma frequency, and time–frequency drift diagnostics.
general_quotes: The dominant features in the dynamic spectrum observed by Wind/WAVES at frequencies below 2 MHz are two groups of type III bursts, labelled III1 and III2.

data_collection_periods.period_name: Low-frequency signatures during flare stages (III1 and III2)
time_quotes: The dominant features in the dynamic spectrum observed by Wind/WAVES at frequencies below 2 MHz are two groups of type III bursts, labelled III1 and III2.
wavelength_quotes: observed by Wind/WAVES at frequencies below 2 MHz
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: DH–km type III groups associated with stage 1 and stage 2 flare energy release
physobs_quotes: They occurred in association with the SXR and microwave emissions of stages 1 and 2, respectively, and with the two different parts of the Hα flare.
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: These emissions align with extrapolated CME liftoff times.

time_quotes: The spectrum shows a chain of narrow-band emissions with negative frequency drift, indicating the type II bursts, followed by the high-frequency part of type III3 between 11:28 and 11:40 UT.
data_collection_periods.wavelengths: Starting frequency 0.6 MHz; TNR analysis 35–256 kHz; local fpe ~35 kHz; Langmuir packets near 32 kHz
wavelength_quotes: Well after the decay of the SXR and microwave emission a third group of bursts (III3 in Figure 3) is identified (near 11:30 UT), with unusually low starting frequency (0.6 MHz)
The narrow-band short bursts near 32 kHz are Langmuir wave packets.
The open triangles show the time of maximum of the burst at each frequency in the range 35-256 kHz.
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: Short, fast-drifting type III bursts indicating rapid electron escape; type II lane continuation/merging; local plasma frequency evolution
physobs_quotes: The time profiles show that the peak times are not distinguishable over a large part of the frequency spectrum with 1-min integrated data, but that the centre of gravity of the brightest feature shifts to later times at the lower frequencies.
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: TNR enabled precise timing and drift analysis; emission linked to CME interaction altitudes.

instruments.name: SOHO/LASCO Coronagraph on board SOHO
instruments.general_comments: LASCO white-light coronagraphy provided CME detection, sky-plane speeds, liftoff chronology, and CME front heliocentric distances vital to interaction timing and comparison with radio starting frequencies.
general_quotes: Two CMEs were observed in close succession. A sequence of difference images from the Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph (LASCO) aboard the SOHO spacecraft (Brueckner et al., 1995) is displayed in Figure 2

time_quotes: the first CME (henceforth CME1) is seen in the image at 09:30 UT in the north-western quadrant. While it travelled through the corona, the second, broader CME (CME2) appeared underneath (image at 09:54 UT).
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: CME plane-of-sky speeds; halo CME classification
physobs_quotes: Speeds of, respectively, 2094 and 2547 km s−1 were derived from linear fits to the trajectories of their fronts published in the CME catalogue.
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: These kinematics anchor the radio–CME association and interaction timing.

data_collection_periods.period_name: CME front heights and formal intersection
time_quotes: From the LASCO observations and the uncertainties resulting from the straight-line fits to the CME front trajectories, the heliocentric distances of the CME fronts at 11:30 UT are, respectively, (26.9 ± 4.8) R⊙and (24.5 ± 5.5) R⊙.
Formally the CME fronts described by the fits intersected near 12:32 UT at a heliocentric distance of about 38 R⊙.
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: CME interaction geometry consistent with radio starting frequency heights
physobs_quotes: The burst group III3 is hence consistent with harmonic emission from the vicinity of the CME fronts.
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: LASCO heights corroborate type III3 source altitudes.

instruments.name: GOES X-ray Sensor (XRS) on board GOES
instruments.general_comments: GOES SXR fluxes were used to define flare stages, timing, and peak flux for correlation with radio bursts and microwave emission.
general_quotes: The solid blue curve displays the SXR time history (0.1-0.8 nm), using GOES on line data (http//www.sel.noaa.gov/ftpmenu/indices), describing thermal emission from the flare-heated plasma.

time_quotes: The SXR time profile had an initial smooth increase between 06:59 UT and 09:05 UT. Subsequently the SXR flux rose slightly faster until 09:45 UT (stage 1)
wavelength_quotes: The solid blue curve displays the SXR time history (0.1-0.8 nm)
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: Soft X-ray flux evolution delineating stage 1
physobs_quotes: The two stages of the flare identified in the Hα observations in Figure 1 correspond to two distinct events of energy release seen in the SXR and microwave time profiles (Figure 3).
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: Stage 1 coincides with Type III1 activity.

time_quotes: and even faster (stage 2) until the X3.8 peak at 09:52 UT.
wavelength_quotes: The solid blue curve displays the SXR time history (0.1-0.8 nm)
physobs_quotes: until the X3.8 peak at 09:52 UT.
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: Stage 2 coincides with Type III2 and onset of DH type II2.

instruments.name: RSTN (San Vito Solar Observatory) on board [Facility: Radio Solar Telescope Network]
instruments.general_comments: 15.4 GHz microwave time histories were used to track nonthermal electron bursts corresponding to both flare stages and to align with SXR and radio spectral features.
general_quotes: The red curve is the microwave time history at 15.4 GHz, produced by non thermal electrons (energies >100 keV) in magnetic fields of a few hundred G; these were obtained from the San Vito Solar Observatory of the Radio Solar Telescope Network (RSTN) (Guidice et al., 1981)2.

wavelength_quotes: The red curve is the microwave time history at 15.4 GHz
physobs_quotes: The gradual rise in stage 1 and the faster rise in stage 2 were each accompanied by strong microwave bursts.
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: RHESSI was in Earth’s shadow during this burst.

wavelength_quotes: The red curve is the microwave time history at 15.4 GHz
physobs_quotes: The second burst was also observed in hard X-rays by RHESSI3 (Lin et al., 2002)4.

instruments.name: ACE/EPAM (CA60 B detector and LEFS60) on board ACE
instruments.general_comments: EPAM provided high-resolution energetic electron intensities (38–315 keV) and pitch-angle distributions (45–312 keV), used to identify two significant rises related to the flare/CME stages and subsequent CME interaction.
general_quotes: We use high-resolution intensities of magnetically deflected electrons (DE) in the energy range 38-315 keV measured by the B detector of the CA60 telescope of the EPAM experiment (Electron, Proton and Alpha Monitor; Gold et al., 1998) on board ACE, and measurements of the angular distributions in the energy range 45-312 keV detected by the sunward looking telescope LEFS60.

data_collection_periods.period_name: First significant rise of energetic electrons
time_quotes: we found the first significant rise of the electron intensities to occur at 10:00 UT.
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: Near-relativistic electron intensity enhancement and onset of anisotropic PADs
physobs_quotes: Statistically significant PADs are detected first at about 11:00 UT.
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: No clear velocity dispersion; onset criterion >2σ above background.

data_collection_periods.period_name: Second rise associated with CME interaction
time_quotes: Extrapolation of this second rise to the pre-event background intensities indicates a start at ≈12:00 UT.
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: Stronger unidirectional anisotropies indicating fresh electron injection
physobs_quotes: The electron PADs (inset b in Figure 9) indicate stronger unidirectional anisotropies are observed in association with this electron enhancement, which provides evidence for fresh injection of energetic electrons between the Sun and the spacecraft.
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: Timing consistent with type III3-produced electron escape.

instruments.name: ACE/SWEPAM on board ACE
instruments.general_comments: SWEPAM solar wind speeds were used to compute Parker spiral path lengths and infer electron release times for both early rise and CME interaction intervals.
general_quotes: for the measured solar wind speed of 620 km s−1 (ACE/SWEPAM) at the time of the rise of the electron intensity had a length of about 1.05 AU

physobs_quotes: we calculated that the nominal Parker spiral for the measured solar wind speed of 620 km s−1 (ACE/SWEPAM) at the time of the rise of the electron intensity had a length of about 1.05 AU
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: Used to estimate ~15 min travel time for 100 keV electrons.

data_collection_periods.time_range: 2005-01-17 ~11:37 – 11:46 UT (context of type III3 and release)
time_quotes: the path travelled to the spacecraft along the nominal Parker spiral is 0.92 AU for the solar wind speed measured at the time of type III3 (800 km/s).

instruments.name: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory (Hα) on board [Facility: Kanzelhöhe Observatory]
instruments.general_comments: Hα imaging was used to define flare timing, staging, ribbon and filament evolution in AR 10720, correlating with SXR and radio activity.
general_quotes: Figure 1 displays snapshots in the Hα line obtained from the Kanzelh¨ohe solar observatory (courtesy M. Temmer; see also Temmer et al. (2007), their figure 2, for details on the evolution of the Hα flare ribbons).

time_quotes: The most conspicuous event was a 3B Hα flare reported by Kanzelh¨ohe 09:16-11:57 UT.
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: Two-stage flare ribbon evolution and filament eruptions in AR 10720
physobs_quotes: The two stages of the event were also found in the soft X-ray (SXR) and radio emissions, as will be discussed below.
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: Stage snapshots at 09:13 UT and 09:54 UT illustrate spatial evolution.
